components.note: 页 (page, head) — originally a head; now a page, as in 页码 page number. As radical it marks the head or face, as in 顶, 领, 额.

example.pinyin: Qǐng fān dào dì shí yè.
example.english: Please turn to page ten.
example.fact: 页 counts the pages of a book (第十页) and has carried over to the digital world: 网页 is a web page and 首页 is a home page. It is a different word from 叶 (leaf), which is pronounced exactly the same, yè.

examples.hanzi: 请翻到下一页。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng fāndào xià yí yè.
examples.english: Please turn to the next page.

examples.hanzi: 这本书有两百页。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu liǎngbǎi yè.
examples.english: This book has two hundred pages.

meanings: to sign (one's name with a pen etc)

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ⺮ is bamboo, as in 笔, 筷, 箱; slips of bamboo were written on, so 签 is a slip or to sign.
佥 (qiān) — same sound — 签 is qiān; 佥 also sounds out 检 jiǎn and 脸 liǎn.
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ qiānmíng.
example.english: Please sign here.
example.fact: 签's bamboo radical ⺮ reflects its original meaning, a bamboo slip or tally used as a marker or a lot-drawing stick in ancient China — 签名 extends that old idea of a marked, identifying token into the modern act of writing one's name to authenticate something.

examples.hanzi: 他在书上给我签名了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shū shang gěi wǒ qiānmíng le.
examples.english: He signed his name in my book.

examples.hanzi: 这是我最喜欢的歌手的签名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ zuì xǐhuan de gēshǒu de qiānmíng.
examples.english: This is the signature of my favorite singer.

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
尚 (shàng) — 尚 itself gives the sound shàng to 赏 shǎng, 掌 zhǎng and 常 cháng.

example.hanzi: 这个牌子的衣服很时尚。
example.pinyin: Zhège páizi de yīfu hěn shíshàng.
example.english: This brand's clothes are very fashionable.
example.fact: 时 contributes "the times, the present era" (the same root behind 时间 and 时候), and 尚 carries a sense of "to esteem, hold in high regard" — 时尚 literally reads close to "what the times esteem," a fitting compositional image for "fashion, trend."

examples.hanzi: 她穿得很时尚。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān de hěn shíshàng.
examples.english: She dresses very fashionably.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢看时尚杂志。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan kàn shíshàng zázhì.
examples.english: He likes reading fashion magazines.

components.note: 白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 如果明天不下雨的话,我们就去爬山。
example.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān bú xiàyǔ dehuà, wǒmen jiù qù páshān.
example.english: If it doesn't rain tomorrow, we'll go hiking.
example.fact: 的话 tacks onto the end of a conditional clause to mark it as hypothetical, and it very often pairs redundantly with a leading 如果 ("if") — "如果...的话" double-marks the same "if" meaning at both ends of the clause, much like "因为...所以" keeps both halves in earlier batches of this deck.

examples.hanzi: 你要是累的话,就先休息吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yàoshi lèi de huà, jiù xiān xiūxi ba.
examples.english: If you're tired, just rest first.

examples.hanzi: 想去的话,明天就出发。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎng qù de huà, míngtiān jiù chūfā.
examples.english: If you want to go, we'll set off tomorrow.

components.note: 文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.
音 (sound) — 音 over 十 — a full piece of music, so a section; 章 sounds out 彰 zhāng and 障 zhàng.

example.hanzi: 他写了一篇很好的文章。
example.pinyin: Tā xiěle yì piān hěn hǎo de wénzhāng.
example.english: He wrote a very good article.
example.fact: 文 depicts a chest marked with crossing patterns or tattoos, an old image of decoration that broadened into "writing, culture" — 文章 combines "writing" with 章 ("chapter, composition") into a word that names a complete, structured piece of writing.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章写得很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng xiě de hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This article is very interesting.

examples.hanzi: 老师让我们写一篇关于家乡的文章。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī ràng wǒmen xiě yì piān guānyú jiāxiāng de wénzhāng.
examples.english: The teacher asked us to write an essay about our hometown.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
木 (wood) — wooden things: 桌, 板, 桥; 架 is a wooden frame or rack.
加 (jiā) is a near sound match for jià; also in 驾 jià and 嘉 jiā.

example.pinyin: Nà liǎng gè háizi yòu dǎjià le.
example.english: Those two kids got into a fight again.
example.fact: 架 in 打架 doesn't mean its usual "frame, rack" (as in 书架, "bookshelf") — it's a fossilized object noun bound only to 打, the same way 天 is fixed as the object of 聊 in 聊天 (also in this batch); neither noun can be swapped for a synonym.

examples.hanzi: 他们小时候经常打架,现在是好朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen xiǎoshíhou jīngcháng dǎjià, xiànzài shì hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: They often fought as kids and are good friends now.

examples.hanzi: 学校不允许学生打架。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào bù yǔnxǔ xuésheng dǎjià.
examples.english: The school doesn't allow students to fight.

components.note: 疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.
龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìngdú chuánbò de hěn kuài.
example.english: This virus spreads very quickly.
example.fact: 病毒 was coined as a direct calque of the Western biomedical concept "virus," pairing 病 ("illness, disease") with 毒 ("poison, toxin") — and the same word does double duty for both a biological virus and a computer virus, just as "virus" does in English.

examples.hanzi: 我的电脑中了病毒,打不开了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de diànnǎo zhòng le bìngdú, dǎ bù kāi le.
examples.english: My computer got a virus and won't open.

examples.hanzi: 这种病毒可以通过空气传播。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìngdú kěyǐ tōngguò kōngqì chuánbō.
examples.english: This virus can spread through the air.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 财, 买, 费; 赋 first meant a tax to raise soldiers.
武 (wǔ) — loose hint — 赋 is fù.

example.hanzi: 她在音乐方面很有天赋。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuè fāngmiàn hěn yǒu tiānfù.
example.english: She has a lot of talent in music.
example.fact: 赋 originally named a tax or levy exacted by the state (its 贝 "money" component ties to wealth, and its form has old links to military funding) — that sense of something imposed by authority later extended to the opposite direction, "to bestow, grant" (as in 赋予, "to endow with"), and 天赋 uses exactly that extended sense, framing a talent as something granted by heaven rather than earned.

examples.hanzi: 他有画画的天赋。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu huà huà de tiānfù.
examples.english: He has a gift for drawing.

examples.hanzi: 努力比天赋更重要。
examples.pinyin: Nǔlì bǐ tiānfù gèng zhòngyào.
examples.english: Hard work matters more than talent.

components.note: 正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.pinyin: Tā zhěngtiān dōu zài kànshū.
example.english: He reads all day long.
example.fact: 整 carries a core sense of "whole, complete, orderly" that recurs in 整齐 ("neat") and 整理 ("to tidy up") — 整天 simply attaches that "whole" sense to 天 ("day") for "the entire day," the same pattern behind 整年 ("all year") and 整夜 ("all night").

examples.hanzi: 昨天我整天都在家里休息。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ zhěng tiān dōu zài jiā lǐ xiūxi.
examples.english: I rested at home all day yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 她整天笑眯眯的,很受欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhěng tiān xiàomīmī de, hěn shòu huānyíng.
examples.english: She smiles all day and is very popular.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 滩 is a shoal or beach.
难 (nán) — near sound — 滩 is tān; 难 also sounds out 摊 tān.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù hǎitān wán le.
example.english: We went to the beach over the weekend.
example.fact: 滩's 氵 (water) component signals its meaning of a sandbar or shoal at the water's edge, while its phonetic half 难 has drifted far from 滩's modern sound tān — 海滩 simply narrows that general "shoal" sense down to the specific case found by the sea.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在海滩上堆沙子。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài hǎitān shang duī shāzi.
examples.english: The kids are building with sand on the beach.

examples.hanzi: 海滩上有很多人在晒太阳。
examples.pinyin: Hǎitān shang yǒu hěn duō rén zài shài tàiyang.
examples.english: Lots of people are sunbathing on the beach.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talking: 说, 计, 谈; 设 is to set up or plan by instruction.
殳 (shū, hand holding a tool) is only a loose sound clue; also in 投 tóu and 股 gǔ.
田 (field) — the bottom part. 备 is simplified from 備; the dictionary story is a trip to the 田 field to prepare for harvest. Treat it as a memory aid.
夂 (going down, slow step) — the top. Memory aid: heading 夂 to the field 田 to get ready — 准备, 设备.

example.hanzi: 这家工厂的设备很先进。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng de shèbèi hěn xiānjìn.
example.english: This factory's equipment is very advanced.
example.fact: 设 means "to establish, set up" and 备 means "to prepare, get ready" — 设备 combines the two into a word for whatever has been set up and made ready for use, covering everything from factory machinery to household appliances.

examples.hanzi: 这家医院新买了一批先进的设备。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā yīyuàn xīn mǎi le yì pī xiānjìn de shèbèi.
examples.english: This hospital bought a batch of advanced equipment.

examples.hanzi: 健身房的设备很齐全。
examples.pinyin: Jiànshēnfáng de shèbèi hěn qíquán.
examples.english: The gym has a full range of equipment.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 这个消息对他是个很大的打击。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi duì tā shì gè hěn dà de dǎjī.
example.english: This news was a huge blow to him.
example.fact: 打击 covers both a literal physical strike and a figurative psychological blow, the same double duty English "hit" performs in "hit hard" — as a verb it also means "to crack down on" (illegal activity, crime), extending "striking" into an enforcement sense with no single-word English equivalent.

examples.hanzi: 他没有被失败打击,而是继续努力。
examples.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu bèi shībài dǎjī, ér shì jìxù nǔlì.
examples.english: He wasn't discouraged by failure and kept working hard.

examples.hanzi: 政府正在打击网上的骗子。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèngzài dǎjī wǎng shang de piànzi.
examples.english: The government is cracking down on online scammers.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 描 is to draw or trace by hand.
苗 (miáo) — same sound — 描 is miáo, like 苗; 苗 also sounds out 猫 māo.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 述 is following a story along, to narrate.
术 (shù) — same sound — 述 is shù, like 术 (art, technique).

example.hanzi: 请你描述一下事情发生的过程。
example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ miáoshù yíxià shìqing fāshēng de guòchéng.
example.english: Please describe how the incident happened.
example.fact: 描 keeps its core sense "to trace, sketch" (as in 描绘, "to depict") while 述 means "to narrate, recount" — 描述 pairs a visual, sketch-like image with a verbal, storytelling one, a fitting blend for the act of describing something in words.

examples.hanzi: 请你描述一下那个人的样子。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ miáoshù yíxià nà ge rén de yàngzi.
examples.english: Please describe what that person looked like.

examples.hanzi: 她无法用语言描述当时的心情。
examples.pinyin: Tā wúfǎ yòng yǔyán miáoshù dāngshí de xīnqíng.
examples.english: She couldn't describe her feelings at that time in words.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 泡 is bubbles, soaking and steeping, as in 泡茶 make tea.
包 (bāo) — close sound: 泡 pāo. 包 also sounds out 炮 pào and 抱 bào.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng pào bēi chá.
example.english: I want to make a cup of tea.
example.fact: 泡 as a verb means to soak or steep, so you 泡茶 (brew tea), 泡面 (make instant noodles) or 泡温泉 (soak in a hot spring). The reading pāo is a different word meaning puffy or spongy, so check the tone before you say it.

examples.hanzi: 他在洗澡时喜欢泡很久。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài xǐzǎo shí xǐhuan pào hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: He likes to soak for a long time when bathing.

examples.hanzi: 请给我泡一杯热茶。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ pào yì bēi rèchá.
examples.english: Please make me a cup of tea.

meanings: likeness of a god or Buddha

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".

example.pinyin: Miào lǐ gòng zhe yí zuò shénxiàng.
example.english: There's a statue of a god enshrined in the temple.
example.fact: 像 shares its phonetic half 象 with the word for "elephant" purely for the sound xiàng, with no meaning connection between them — 神像 simply combines 神 ("god, deity") with 像's core sense "likeness, image" for a carved or painted representation of a deity.

examples.hanzi: 老人每天早上都向神像鞠躬。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén měi tiān zǎoshang dōu xiàng shénxiàng jūgōng.
examples.english: The old man bows to the statue of the god every morning.

examples.hanzi: 这座古庙里有一千年前的神像。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔmiào lǐ yǒu yì qiān nián qián de shénxiàng.
examples.english: This old temple has a statue of a god from a thousand years ago.

components.note: 医 (doctor) — simplified from 醫, which had 酉 (medicinal wine, as in 酒) at the bottom; the box 匚 and arrow 矢 remain.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and healing: 病, 痛, 症; 疗 is to treat illness.
了 (liǎo) stands in for the sound of traditional 療 (liáo), close to liáo.

example.hanzi: 这家医院提供免费的医疗服务。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yīyuàn tígōng miǎnfèi de yīliáo fúwù.
example.english: This hospital provides free medical services.
example.fact: 医's oldest form is built around 矢 ("arrow"), reflecting its origin in treating battlefield arrow wounds — 医疗 pairs that ancient "healing" root with 疗 ("to cure, treat," itself built on the "sickbed" radical 疒) into the modern word for medical care in general.

examples.hanzi: 农村的医疗条件正在变好。
examples.pinyin: Nóngcūn de yīliáo tiáojiàn zhèngzài biàn hǎo.
examples.english: Medical conditions in rural areas are improving.

examples.hanzi: 医疗费用越来越高了。
examples.pinyin: Yīliáo fèiyòng yuè lái yuè gāo le.
examples.english: Medical costs are getting higher and higher.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — the top. Memory aid: grains of rice sorted by size 大 — sorted into groups, a kind (人类). Not proven etymology.
類 (traditional) — used for 'kind, class' with 犬 and 页. 类 is the simplified shape and keeps only a fragment of it.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 像 resemble; 似 is to look like.
以 (yǐ) is only a loose sound hint for sì.

example.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ de xiǎngfǎ lèisì.
example.english: The two of them have similar ideas.
example.fact: 似 pictures 亻 (a person) doubled, one figure next to another that resembles it — 类似 combines that image with 类 ("category, type") for things similar enough to belong to the same category, a slightly more formal register than the plainer 一样 seen earlier in this deck.

examples.hanzi: 这两个故事很类似。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge gùshi hěn lèisì.
examples.english: These two stories are very similar.

examples.hanzi: 我以前遇到过类似的问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián yùdào guo lèisì de wèntí.
examples.english: I've run into a similar problem before.

components.note: 衣 (clothing, cloth) — clothes and cloth: 装, 被, 衬; 袋 is a bag made of cloth.
代 (dài) sounds exactly like 袋; also in 贷 dài.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de dàizi hěn zhòng.
example.english: My bag is very heavy.
example.fact: 袋 usually shows up with a suffix or partner: 袋子 (bag), 口袋 (pocket), 塑料袋 (plastic bag). It also works as a measure word for bagged goods, as in 一袋米 (a bag of rice). 袋鼠 is the word for kangaroo, literally 'pouch rat'.

examples.hanzi: 她把东西放在一个小袋子里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ dōngxi fàng zài yí gè xiǎo dàizi lǐ.
examples.english: She put the things in a small bag.

examples.hanzi: 我口袋里有一块糖。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kǒudài lǐ yǒu yí kuài táng.
examples.english: I have a piece of candy in my pocket.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院, 队; hiding behind a mound — 隐 is to conceal; the right side is a simplified stand-in.
艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 is grass and plants, as in 花, 草, 菜; hiding under vegetation — 藏 is to conceal or store.
臧 (zāng) — near sound — 藏 is cáng; 臧 also sounds out 脏 zāng.

example.hanzi: 他试图隐藏自己的真实想法。
example.pinyin: Tā shìtú yǐncáng zìjǐ de zhēnshí xiǎngfǎ.
example.english: He tried to hide his true thoughts.
example.fact: 藏's 艹 (grass) component reflects its original image of concealing something among vegetation, while 隐 pictures someone anxiously ducking out of sight behind a mound (阝) — 隐藏 doubles up two independently plausible "hiding" images into one word.

examples.hanzi: 她把钥匙隐藏在花盆下面。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yàoshi yǐncáng zài huāpén xiàmian.
examples.english: She hid the key under the flowerpot.

examples.hanzi: 这个软件可以隐藏你的文件。
examples.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ yǐncáng nǐ de wénjiàn.
examples.english: This software can hide your files.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破, 码, 砖; 硬 is hard.
更 (gēng) is only a loose sound hint for yìng.

example.pinyin: Zhège miànbāo tài yìng le.
example.english: This bread is too hard.
example.fact: 硬 is the opposite of 软 (ruǎn, soft), and it extends beyond texture: 硬座 is a train's hard seat, 硬盘 is a hard drive, and 硬要 means to insist stubbornly on doing something.

examples.hanzi: 这块石头很硬。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài shítou hěn yìng.
examples.english: This stone is very hard.

examples.hanzi: 他很硬气，从不向别人低头。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yìngqi, cóng bù xiàng biéren dītóu.
examples.english: He is tough and never bows to anyone.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 语 is language and spoken words.
吾 (wú) — loose hint — 语 is yǔ; 吾 also sounds out 悟 wù.
言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.pinyin: Tā néng shuō sān zhǒng yǔyán.
example.english: She can speak three languages.
example.fact: 言 is a pictograph of a mouth (口) with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out, an image of speaking, while 语 adds the phonetic 吾 to the same 讠 "speech" radical — 语言 doubles up two independently speech-related characters into the general word for "language."

examples.hanzi: 学习一门新语言需要耐心。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxí yì mén xīn yǔyán xūyào nàixīn.
examples.english: Learning a new language takes patience.

examples.hanzi: 音乐是不分国家的语言。
examples.pinyin: Yīnyuè shì bù fēn guójiā de yǔyán.
examples.english: Music is a language without borders.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 标 first meant the tip of a tree, hence a mark or target; wood radical as in 树 tree, 板 board.
票 (piào) is the sound in traditional 標; same series 漂 piāo and 飘 piāo; simplified 标 now shows 示.
冫 (ice) — cold, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 冻 freeze; here it stands for 氵 water in 準 (a water level, so exact).
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) gives only a loose sound clue for zhǔn.

example.pinyin: Zhè bù fúhé ānquán biāozhǔn.
example.english: This doesn't meet the safety standard.
example.fact: 准's 冫 ("ice/water") component traces back to a carpenter's level that used a pool of water to check flatness — 标准 pairs that "true and level" sense with 标 ("mark, sign") for a fixed, agreed-upon mark other things are measured against.

examples.hanzi: 老师按照同一个标准给分。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī ànzhào tóng yí ge biāozhǔn gěi fēn.
examples.english: The teacher grades by the same standard.

examples.hanzi: 他的中文发音很标准。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Zhōngwén fāyīn hěn biāozhǔn.
examples.english: His Chinese pronunciation is very standard.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.pinyin: Tā duì yīnyuè chōngmǎn jīqíng.
example.english: He is full of passion for music.
example.fact: 激 originally described water dashing forcefully against something (氵 "water" plus the phonetic 敫) — 激情 extends that image of a forceful surge of water to emotion, giving "passion" a literal sense of feeling that rushes and crashes rather than sits still.

examples.hanzi: 她对工作充满了激情。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì gōngzuò chōngmǎn le jīqíng.
examples.english: She is full of passion for her work.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌里有年轻人的激情。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē lǐ yǒu niánqīngrén de jīqíng.
examples.english: This song has the passion of young people.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.
身 (body, bow) — 身 is a worn-down picture of a bow, with a hand 寸 drawing it — 射 is to shoot.

example.hanzi: 医生给他做了一次注射。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi tā zuòle yí cì zhùshè.
example.english: The doctor gave him an injection.
example.fact: 注 keeps its core sense "to pour" (as in 注意, literally "to pour one's mind [into something]"), and 射 pictures a drawn bow (身) with a hand releasing the arrow (寸) — 注射 combines "to pour" with "to shoot," a fittingly forceful image for pushing liquid into the body with a needle.

examples.hanzi: 这种药要注射,不能吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào yào zhùshè, bù néng chī.
examples.english: This medicine needs to be injected, not taken orally.

examples.hanzi: 护士正在给孩子注射疫苗。
examples.pinyin: Hùshi zhèngzài gěi háizi zhùshè yìmiáo.
examples.english: The nurse is giving the child a vaccine injection.

components.note: 车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Tā gāng mǎile yí liàng xīn chēzi.
example.english: He just bought a new car.
example.fact: 车 is a simplified form of 車, itself a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above, wheels and axle visible in the shape — 子 here is the same light, semantically bleached suffix seen in 孩子 (also in this deck), turning the bare noun "cart, vehicle" into the everyday colloquial word for one.

examples.hanzi: 这辆车子开起来很稳。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chēzi kāi qǐlái hěn wěn.
examples.english: This car drives very smoothly.

examples.hanzi: 他的车子坏了,得去修一下。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chēzi huài le, děi qù xiū yíxià.
examples.english: His car broke down and needs to be repaired.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — liquids and flow: 河, 汤, 酒; 治 first meant controlling water, then governing and curing.
台 (tái) is only a loose sound hint; the same part is in 始 shǐ and 胎 tāi.

example.pinyin: Yīshēng néng zhìhǎo nǐ de bìng.
example.english: The doctor can cure your illness.
example.fact: 治 covers two worlds: running a state (政治, 治国) and treating illness (治病, 治疗). The legend of 大禹治水, Yu the Great taming the floods, shows the water radical's original link to managing rivers.

examples.hanzi: 医生治好了他的病。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng zhì hǎo le tā de bìng.
examples.english: The doctor cured his illness.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家治理得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā zhìlǐ de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This country is governed very well.

components.note: 门 (gate, door) — 门 is a gate, as in 开, 关, 问; 阁 is a pavilion with doors.
各 (gè) — same sound — 阁 is gé; 各 also sounds out 格 gé and 胳 gē.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.pinyin: Géxià, qǐng wǎng zhè biān zǒu.
example.english: Your excellency, please come this way.
example.fact: 阁 originally named a raised pavilion or high building (as in 阁楼, "attic"), and 下 here works like the "below" in English "Your Highness" — 阁下 literally addresses someone as speaking from "below your tower," an indirect, deferential way of naming a person of high rank without naming them directly.

examples.hanzi: 阁下的到来让我们感到十分荣幸。
examples.pinyin: Géxià de dàolái ràng wǒmen gǎndào shífēn róngxìng.
examples.english: Your presence is a great honor for us.

examples.hanzi: 请问阁下贵姓?
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn géxià guì xìng?
examples.english: May I ask your honorable name, sir?

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 他把这只猫当作自己的孩子。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhè zhī māo dàngzuò zìjǐ de háizi.
example.english: He treats this cat as if it were his own child.
example.fact: 当 here takes its less common fourth-tone reading dàng ("to regard as, to treat as"), not the far more frequent first-tone dāng ("to act as, when," as in 当时) — mixing up the two tones is an easy, common slip for learners meeting 当作 for the first time.

examples.hanzi: 别把我的话当作玩笑。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ wǒ de huà dàngzuò wánxiào.
examples.english: Don't take my words as a joke.

examples.hanzi: 他把这份工作当作一次学习的机会。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhè fèn gōngzuò dàngzuò yí cì xuéxí de jīhuì.
examples.english: He treats this job as a chance to learn.

components.note: 工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bàba zài gōngchǎng gōngzuò.
example.english: My dad works in a factory.
example.fact: 工 rarely stands alone in modern Chinese; it builds words such as 工作 (job), 工人 (worker), 工资 (wages) and 打工 (to work a casual or part-time job). It is also the radical in 左, 巧 and 差.

examples.hanzi: 他在工厂做工。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngchǎng zuògōng.
examples.english: He works in a factory.

examples.hanzi: 这份工作很辛苦。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò hěn xīnkǔ.
examples.english: This job is very hard.

components.note: 南 (nán) — south; as a part it sounds out 楠 nán and 喃 nán.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài chéngshì de nánbian.
example.english: My home is on the south side of the city.
example.fact: Chinese lists the directions as 东南西北 (east, south, west, north), not north-south-east-west. A compass is 指南针, literally the 'south-pointing needle', and 南 appears in 南方 (the south) and 南京 (Nanjing, 'southern capital').

examples.hanzi: 他住在南京，不在北京。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhù zài Nánjīng, bú zài Běijīng.
examples.english: He lives in Nanjing, not Beijing.

examples.hanzi: 冬天鸟儿都飞到南方去了。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān niǎor dōu fēi dào nánfāng qù le.
examples.english: In winter the birds all fly to the south.

components.note: 宀 (roof, house) — a house family: 家 home, 安 safe, 室 room. 奥 originally meant the inner, dark corner of a house, hence 'mysterious, profound'.
米 (rice) — in the middle; the dictionary's story is a person finding a house full of rice. Memory aid, not proven.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: something big and hidden deep inside the house is mysterious.

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de nèiróng hěn shēn'ào.
example.english: The content of this book is very profound.
example.fact: 奥 almost never stands alone. It appears in 深奥 (profound), 奥妙 (mystery, subtlety), 奥运会 (the Olympics) and 奥地利 (Austria). Its oldest meaning was the deep inner corner of a house, which fits the idea of something hidden and hard to reach.

examples.hanzi: 这道数学题很奥妙。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào shùxué tí hěn àomiào.
examples.english: This math problem is quite subtle.

examples.hanzi: 奥运会每四年开一次。
examples.pinyin: Àoyùnhuì měi sì nián kāi yí cì.
examples.english: The Olympic Games are held every four years.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: giving permission is spoken.
午 (wǔ) is only a loose sound clue for xǔ.

example.pinyin: Tā yěxǔ míngtiān huì lái.
example.english: Maybe he will come tomorrow.
example.fact: 许 mostly lives inside compounds: 也许 and 或许 (perhaps), 允许 (to permit), 许多 (many). It is also a common surname, Xǔ, and can mean 'to promise', as in 许愿 (to make a wish).

examples.hanzi: 学校不许学生迟到。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào bù xǔ xuésheng chídào.
examples.english: The school doesn't allow students to be late.

examples.hanzi: 许多人都来参加了。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō rén dōu lái cānjiā le.
examples.english: Many people came to take part.

components.note: 女 (woman) — marks women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 好 good; 娶 is a man taking a wife.
取 (qǔ) — same sound: 娶 qǔ. 取 means take: to take a woman as wife.

example.pinyin: Tā míngnián yào qǔ tā.
example.english: He is going to marry her next year.
example.fact: Chinese has separate verbs for each side of a wedding: a man 娶 (takes) a wife, a woman 嫁 (jià) marries into a husband's family. You cannot swap them; in English both are just 'to marry'.

examples.hanzi: 他想娶她做妻子。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qǔ tā zuò qīzi.
examples.english: He wants to marry her as his wife.

examples.hanzi: 他娶了一位很好的姑娘。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǔ le yí wèi hěn hǎo de gūniang.
examples.english: He married a very nice girl.

components.note: 文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.

example.pinyin: Nǐ huì xiě Zhōngwén ma?
example.english: Can you write Chinese?
example.fact: 文 names languages in their written form: 中文, 英文, 日文. 语, as in 汉语 and 英语, leans toward the spoken language, though the two are often interchangeable. 文 also underlies 文化 (culture) and 文明 (civilization).

examples.hanzi: 我在学中文。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài xué Zhōngwén.
examples.english: I'm learning Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This article is very interesting.

meanings: to be in (some state, position, or condition)

components.note: 夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 这个国家目前处于经济危机之中。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā mùqián chǔyú jīngjì wēijī zhī zhōng.
example.english: This country is currently in an economic crisis.
example.fact: 处 here takes its third-tone reading chǔ ("to deal with, to be situated," as in 处理), not the fourth-tone chù used for its noun sense "place, location" (as in 到处, "everywhere") — the same character splits cleanly between a "place" reading and a "to be positioned/deal with" reading depending on tone.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司目前处于发展阶段。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī mùqián chǔyú fāzhǎn jiēduàn.
examples.english: This company is currently in a growth stage.

examples.hanzi: 这座山处于两个省的交界处。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò shān chǔyú liǎng ge shěng de jiāojiè chù.
examples.english: This mountain is located at the border of two provinces.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical, as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 犹 first named an animal.
尤 (yóu) — same sound — 犹 is yóu, like 尤; 尤 also sounds out 优 yōu.
大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他的很多朋友都是犹太人。
example.pinyin: Tā de hěn duō péngyou dōu shì Yóutàirén.
example.english: Many of his friends are Jewish.
example.fact: 犹太 is a phonetic transliteration of "Judea/Judah," with 犹 and 太 chosen purely for their sound and carrying no meaning of their own here — 人 ("person") is simply appended the same way it is in 中国人 or 美国人 to turn a place or people name into "a person of that people."

examples.hanzi: 这位教授是犹太人,出生在欧洲。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi jiàoshòu shì Yóutàirén, chūshēng zài Ōuzhōu.
examples.english: This professor is Jewish and was born in Europe.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市里有一个犹太人社区。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì lǐ yǒu yí ge Yóutàirén shèqū.
examples.english: There is a Jewish community in this city.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.

example.pinyin: Qǐng xiě yí fèn lùnwén tíyào.
example.english: Please write an abstract for the paper.
example.fact: 提 keeps its core sense "to lift, raise, bring up" (as in 提问, "to raise a question"), and 要 here means "the essentials, the important points" — 提要 literally "to draw out the essentials," a fittingly literal name for a document that extracts a text's key points.

examples.hanzi: 请在论文前面写一个提要。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài lùnwén qiánmiàn xiě yí ge tíyào.
examples.english: Please write an abstract at the front of the paper.

examples.hanzi: 这份提要只有两百个字。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn tíyào zhǐ yǒu liǎng bǎi ge zì.
examples.english: This summary is only two hundred characters long.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 投 is to throw.
殳 (shū) is a weapon-in-hand part that is only a loose sound clue; it also appears in 设 shè and 段 duàn.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买; 资 is capital or resources.
次 (cì) is a loose clue; same part in 姿 zī and 咨 zī.

example.hanzi: 他把钱投资在了房地产上。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ qián tóuzī zàile fángdìchǎn shàng.
example.english: He invested his money in real estate.
example.fact: 投 keeps its core sense "to throw, to cast" (as in 投球, "to throw a ball"), so 投资 literally pictures "throwing" one's 资 (funds, capital) into something — a vivid, if slightly risky-sounding, image for the act of investing.

examples.hanzi: 他想投资一家新公司。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng tóuzī yì jiā xīn gōngsī.
examples.english: He wants to invest in a new company.

examples.hanzi: 这个项目需要很大的投资。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù xūyào hěn dà de tóuzī.
examples.english: This project requires a large investment.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng shuō yǒudiǎn guòfèn le.
example.english: What you just said is a bit excessive.
example.fact: 过 carries a core sense of "to pass, to cross over" (as in 过去, "to pass by, the past"), so 过分 literally means "to cross over the [proper] division" (分) — going past the line that marks what's reasonable or appropriate.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试的要求有点过分严格。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì de yāoqiú yǒudiǎn guòfèn yángé.
examples.english: The requirements of this exam are a bit too strict.

examples.hanzi: 你不要太过分,我已经让步了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào tài guòfèn, wǒ yǐjīng ràngbù le.
examples.english: Don't go too far, I've already given way.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.

example.hanzi: 他还没有女朋友,一直在找对象。
example.pinyin: Tā hái méiyǒu nǚpéngyou, yìzhí zài zhǎo duìxiàng.
example.english: He doesn't have a girlfriend yet — he's still looking for a partner.
example.fact: 对象 covers both a neutral, abstract sense ("target, object [of study or action]") and a distinctly colloquial one, "boyfriend or girlfriend" — 找对象 ("to look for a partner") is the standard, extremely common way to talk about dating and marriage prospects in everyday Mandarin.

examples.hanzi: 他在找结婚的对象。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhǎo jiéhūn de duìxiàng.
examples.english: He is looking for someone to marry.

examples.hanzi: 这个节目的对象是小学生。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiémù de duìxiàng shì xiǎoxuéshēng.
examples.english: This program is aimed at elementary school students.

meanings: to see each other for a bit

components.note: 见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǎo gè shíjiān jiàn jian ba.
example.english: Let's find some time to meet up.
example.fact: 见见 reduplicates the single verb 见 ("to see, to meet") to soften and shorten the action into "meet for a bit" — the same casual reduplication pattern behind 看看 ("take a look") and 想想 ("think it over"), which is why the second syllable's tone typically flattens to neutral in speech (jiàn jian, not jiàn jiàn).

examples.hanzi: 好久没见了,我们见见面吧。
examples.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ méi jiàn le, wǒmen jiànjian miàn ba.
examples.english: We haven't met for a long time, so let's get together.

examples.hanzi: 我想去见见老朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù jiànjian lǎo péngyou.
examples.english: I want to go see my old friends.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
至 (zhì) — same sound — 致 is zhì, like 至 (to arrive); 致 is to cause to arrive, then to bring about.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action performed, as in 教, 放, 收.

example.pinyin: Dàjiā de yìjiàn hěn yízhì.
example.english: Everyone's opinions are very much in agreement.
example.fact: 一致 attaches 一 ("one") to 致 ("to arrive at, bring about") for a literal "arriving at one [point]" — the compositional image behind the modern sense "in agreement, unanimous," much like English "come to one mind" describes the same convergence.

examples.hanzi: 大家的想法完全一致。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā de xiǎngfǎ wánquán yízhì.
examples.english: Everyone's thinking is exactly the same.

examples.hanzi: 他说的和做的不一致。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de hé zuò de bù yízhì.
examples.english: What he says and what he does are inconsistent.

components.note: 月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn qīdài zhè cì lǚxíng.
example.english: I'm really looking forward to this trip.
example.fact: 期 turns up in time words: 星期 (week), 日期 (date), 学期 (semester), 假期 (holiday). It can also be a measure word for issues or installments, as in 第三期. 期待 means to look forward to something with anticipation.

examples.hanzi: 我们下一期再见。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xià yì qī zàijiàn.
examples.english: See you in the next issue.

examples.hanzi: 学期结束了，我们放暑假。
examples.pinyin: Xuéqī jiéshù le, wǒmen fàng shǔjià.
examples.english: The semester has ended and we have summer vacation.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — allowances and payments, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
占 (zhàn) is only a loose sound clue for tiē.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhàopiàn tiē zài zhèlǐ.
example.english: Please stick the photo here.
example.fact: 贴 means to stick something flat onto a surface: 贴纸 is a sticker and 贴邮票 is to put on a stamp. 贴心 literally 'close to the heart', describes someone considerate. Online, 贴 is also used for forum posts, as in Baidu's 贴吧.

examples.hanzi: 请在信封上贴邮票。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài xìnfēng shang tiē yóupiào.
examples.english: Please stick a stamp on the envelope.

examples.hanzi: 他在墙上贴了一张海报。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài qiáng shang tiē le yì zhāng hǎibào.
examples.english: He put a poster on the wall.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.
禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 移 first meant grain swaying, then shifting and moving.
多 (duō) — the original sound clue — today 移 yí is only loosely related to 多 duō.

example.hanzi: 医生把病人转移到了另一间病房。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng bǎ bìngrén zhuǎnyí dàole lìng yì jiān bìngfáng.
example.english: The doctor transferred the patient to another ward.
example.fact: 转 keeps its core sense "to turn, to change direction" (车, "cart," reflecting the image of a turning wheel), and 移 independently means "to move, shift" — 转移 combines "turning" with "moving" for relocating something, whether a patient, funds, or someone's attention.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司把工厂转移到了南方。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī bǎ gōngchǎng zhuǎnyí dào le nánfāng.
examples.english: This company moved its factory to the south.

examples.hanzi: 老师想转移孩子的注意力。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī xiǎng zhuǎnyí háizi de zhùyìlì.
examples.english: The teacher wants to shift the child's attention.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.pinyin: Tā fùzé guǎnlǐ zhè jiā gōngsī.
example.english: He's in charge of managing this company.
example.fact: 管 originally named a bamboo pipe or tube (⺮, "bamboo"), later extending metaphorically to "to control, to be in charge of" — much as English "channel" can drift from a literal waterway to an organizational sense, 管 drifted from a physical tube to administrative oversight.

examples.hanzi: 她很会管理自己的时间。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn huì guǎnlǐ zìjǐ de shíjiān.
examples.english: She is good at managing her time.

examples.hanzi: 这个小区的物业管理很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎoqū de wùyè guǎnlǐ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The property management in this community is very good.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: hidden indoors, secret.
宓 (mì) gives the exact sound; also in 蜜 mì.

example.hanzi: 这份文件的内容必须保密。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn wénjiàn de nèiróng bìxū bǎomì.
example.english: The contents of this document must be kept confidential.
example.fact: 保 keeps its core sense "to protect, look after" (its own etymology traces to a caretaker cradling a child), and 密 means "dense, secret, close" — 保密 literally "to protect the secret," treating confidentiality as something actively guarded rather than just withheld.

examples.hanzi: 请你替我保密,不要告诉别人。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ tì wǒ bǎomì, bú yào gàosu biérén.
examples.english: Please keep it secret for me and don't tell anyone.

examples.hanzi: 这个计划目前还在保密阶段。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà mùqián hái zài bǎomì jiēduàn.
examples.english: This plan is still at the confidential stage.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摆 is to arrange or swing with the hands.
罢 (bà) — near sound — 摆 is bǎi, matching 罢.
月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 脱 is slipping off a layer, like skin or clothes.
兑 (duì) — near sound — 脱 is tuō; 兑 also sounds out 说 shuō and 税 shuì.

example.hanzi: 他终于摆脱了那份压力很大的工作。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú bǎituō le nà fèn yālì hěn dà de gōngzuò.
example.english: He finally freed himself from that very stressful job.
example.fact: 摆 (扌 "hand" + phonetic 罢) means "to swing, to place," and 脱 (⺼ "flesh, body" + phonetic 兑) literally means "to take something off the body," like shedding clothing — combined, 摆脱 pictures physically shaking something off, extended metaphorically to breaking free from a burden or bad situation.

examples.hanzi: 我想摆脱这种不规律的生活。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎituō zhè zhǒng bù guīlǜ de shēnghuó.
examples.english: I want to get away from this irregular lifestyle.

examples.hanzi: 他怎么也摆脱不了那个坏习惯。
examples.pinyin: Tā zěnme yě bǎituō bù liǎo nàge huài xíguàn.
examples.english: He just can't shake that bad habit.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 男, 努; 助 is to lend strength.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 姐 jiě.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 她是医生的助手,负责整理病历。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yīshēng de zhùshǒu, fùzé zhěnglǐ bìnglì.
example.english: She is the doctor's assistant, responsible for organizing medical records.
example.fact: 助手 combines 助 ("to help," built from 力 "strength") with 手 ("hand") into a nearly literal "helping hand" — the same image English reaches for with its own idiom "right-hand man."

examples.hanzi: 我需要一个助手来帮我整理文件。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào yí ge zhùshǒu lái bāng wǒ zhěnglǐ wénjiàn.
examples.english: I need an assistant to help me organize files.

examples.hanzi: 他在实验室里当老师的助手。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shíyànshì lǐ dāng lǎoshī de zhùshǒu.
examples.english: He works as the teacher's helper in the lab.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — 鬼 is a ghost or spirit, as in 魂, 魔; 魅 is a spirit that bewitches.
未 (wèi) — near sound — 魅 is mèi; 未 also sounds out 妹 mèi.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 这位演员的舞台魅力吸引了很多观众。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi yǎnyuán de wǔtái mèilì xīyǐn le hěn duō guānzhòng.
example.english: This actor's stage charisma attracted many audience members.
example.fact: 魅 pictures a 鬼 ("ghost, spirit") lurking among 未 (young tree branches) and originally meant "demon, enchanting spirit" — so 魅力, built on that character, frames charisma as an almost supernatural, bewitching pull rather than ordinary attractiveness.

examples.hanzi: 这座古城充满了独特的魅力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔchéng chōngmǎn le dútè de mèilì.
examples.english: This ancient city is full of unique charm.

examples.hanzi: 他的魅力不在外表,而在性格。
examples.pinyin: Tā de mèilì bú zài wàibiǎo, ér zài xìnggé.
examples.english: His charm lies not in his looks but in his personality.
